column7: Both WebAuthn login paths (FinishWebAuthnLogin, FinishWebAuthnPasswordlessLogin) minted the session and an unconditional ambient MFAStepUpGrant (Purpose = MFAStepUpPurposeRestrictedSecretRead) and only THEN handed back to the HTTP handler, which resolved the response identity (GetUserIdentity -> GetUserRoles + GetUserPermissions) for its body. A failure in THAT read was reported to the caller as a failed login (HTTP 500) while both writes stayed: completeLogin revoked the session but nothing revoked the grant, so a step-up grant outlived a login the caller was told had failed -- satisfying the restricted-secret MFA gate for the rest of the step-up window on some later session the user never proved a second factor for. Found by FuzzStorageFaultOperations (op="REST POST /auth/webauthn/login/finish", fault=(GetUserRoles, NthCall=1, kind=error)), confirmed by byte-for-byte replay against unmodified origin/main, and tolerated as an oracle (a) known-open entry until this fix (that tolerance row is removed by the same change). Fixed by ORDERING, not a second compensation: core.resolveLoginIdentityBeforeMint performs the read before the session/grant/step-up-token writes and returns the identity, which the handler uses via completeLoginWithIdentity instead of re-reading -- so no fallible-and-reported step runs after the writes and there is no partial state to undo. New sentinel core.ErrLoginIdentityUnavailable keeps the caller-visible shape identical (same 500, same message) and is deliberately NOT ErrWebAuthnLoginNotEvaluated, so the per-IP login-attempt reservation stays counted exactly as before (the assertion WAS evaluated and passed). Red/green: planting the original shape (read moved back after the grant mint) fires all three arms of the proving test (grant, session, step-up token); planting the intermediate shape (read after mintSession only) fires the session arm; both the passwordless sibling test and the oracle (a) harness with the tolerance removed go red too. Calibration companions stop the fix being made in the wrong direction -- TestFinishWebAuthnLogin_ReturnsAPopulatedIdentityForARoleHolder (the returned identity must be the real one, not UserIdentity{}, which would silently strip every user's roles from the login response) and server/faultops TestWebAuthnLogin_SuccessfulLoginStillMintsItsStepUpGrant (a successful login must still mint the grant; deleting the mint is not the fix). Passwordless path covered by the sibling TestFinishWebAuthnPasswordlessLogin_IdentityReadFailureLeavesNoSessionOrGrant -- that op is not in server/faultops' opCatalog, so its faultops subtest skips with a message naming this core test. SIBLING SWEEP: the same window existed on the TOTP path (VerifyMFALogin, /auth/mfa/verify), which mints no grant but DOES write a user-scoped MFAStepupToken that HasActiveMFAStepup reads per-USER rather than per-session -- same gate, same cross-session reach. Fixed identically and guarded by TestVerifyMFALogin_IdentityReadFailureLeavesNoSessionOrStepUpToken (red on both the token and session arms when the read is moved back after the writes). The remaining two completeLogin callers (Login, ConsumeSetup) write only the session, which completeLogin's existing revoke already covered, so they are unchanged -- established by enumerating what each caller writes after minting, not by assuming the first site found was the only one.
